benchmark.heading: Benchmark
benchmark.heroBlurb: Measure your PC, change something, then re-measure — Compy tells you honestly whether it actually helped. A change smaller than the run-to-run noise reads as “no measurable change,” not a win.
benchmark.rigTierNote: Compy measures against your own rig — scores and verdicts are relative to your saved baseline, not a universal grade. Your tier (rough, from the specs above) keeps any comparison like-to-like: same-class rigs only, never a cross-tier ranking.
benchmark.useCaseBlurb: Tell Compy your main use — it frames what these measurements mean for you. This is just a label saved on this PC: it doesn’t change a single Windows setting, apply a tweak, or touch any service.
benchmark.noBaselineBlurb: Run a benchmark, then save it as your baseline — the fixed point you compare future changes against.
benchmark.calibratePre: With a game running and FPS monitoring on, calibrate — Compy measures your rig's
benchmark.calibratePost: That's the floor: a change smaller than it can't be told apart from noise, so we won't claim it.
benchmark.fpsMonitoringOffMsg: Benchmark needs FPS monitoring — it's off.
benchmark.fpsMonitoringOnMsg: FPS monitoring is on — you're set to measure.
benchmark.measureTweakExplainer: “Measure this tweak” applies the change, measures with it on, then rolls it back — your settings end up exactly as they started. An elevated tweak asks for UAC twice (apply + undo).
benchmark.pipelineCheckPassed: · pipeline check passed (no phantom change across identical runs)
benchmark.noWinsBlurb: No verified wins yet. Measure a tweak above — any change that beats your noise floor lands here. Points are only ever earned by a measured, certified improvement; a tweak that doesn't help earns nothing.
benchmark.localNoPeerCohort: local — your own results, no peer cohort yet
benchmark.awardTraceNote: Every figure here is the raw verdict receipt — no score exists without its measurement.
benchmark.pointsTraceNote: Every point traces to a certified result — the tweak, the metric, and its 95% confidence interval. Nothing is awarded for a change that didn't measurably help.
benchmark.step1: Run a benchmark and set it as your baseline.
benchmark.step2: Change one thing (a Windows setting, or apply one of Compy's tweaks).
benchmark.step3: Re-measure — Compy reports the honest per-part verdict vs your baseline.
benchmark.scoresRelativeNote: Scores are relative (0–100, rough reference) — useful for the comparison, not as an absolute grade.
benchmark.noChangesRecorded: No Compy changes recorded since the baseline — this reflects manual or ambient changes.
benchmark.noiseFloorNote: Changes within ±{{pct}}% are reported as “no measurable change” — below the run-to-run noise floor, so we won’t call them a win or a loss.

trialReason.withinNoise: the change stayed within your rig's run-to-run noise
trialReason.conditionsUnstable: conditions were too noisy to measure reliably — try again
trialReason.invalidTrial: the run was invalid — the GPU throttled or its clock/temperature drifted mid-run — and was discarded

benchmark.attributionCaveatMulti: These {{count}} changes were measured together, so the result is their combined effect — it can't be credited to any one of them.

blackBox.introPre: Black Box reads the crash and freeze evidence Windows already recorded, and overlays Compy's own
blackBox.introPost: from any session that was running at the time. It only reports what was logged — it makes no guesses about the cause.
blackBox.scanErrorMsg: Couldn't read the crash log just now — try again in a moment.
blackBox.emptyWithSkipped: No crashes or freezes in what Compy could read. Some records below need administrator — run Compy as admin to check those too.
blackBox.emptyClean: No crashes or freezes recorded. Either nothing went wrong, or whatever happened left no trace Windows recorded.
blackBox.skippedRunAdmin_one: Run Compy as admin to include this.
blackBox.skippedRunAdmin_other: Run Compy as admin to include these.
blackBox.noVitalsMsg: Compy wasn't monitoring at that moment — no vitals to show.
blackBox.assessLinePostBeyond: — beyond what Compy can safely narrow down.
blackBox.resolvedMark: ✓ You marked this pointed you the right way
blackBox.thanksNoted: Thanks — noted; we'd rather stay quiet than guess wrong.

twoFutures.heading: Two futures
twoFutures.emptyIntro: Run a benchmark before and after a fix to earn this view: your rig as it measured at the baseline, next to how it measures now.
twoFutures.emptyHint: Set a baseline above, change one thing, then re-measure — the split renders only from those two real runs.
twoFutures.noChangesRecorded: No Compy changes recorded since the baseline — this reflects manual or ambient changes.
twoFutures.scoresNote: Relative scores (0–100) from your own two runs — changes within ±{{pct}}% read as “no measurable change”.

rigViewer.dragHint: Drag to orbit · hover or click a part for its live specs
rigViewer.honestyNote: Tailored to your rig — parts and specs read live from your PC. Fans spin at their real RPM when HWiNFO or LibreHardwareMonitor is running; without one they stay faint placeholders. A PSU and the cooler model have no software identity, so they remain ghosts rather than guesses.
rigViewer.nudgeBodyPre: Your fans show as ghosts because Compy stays
rigViewer.nudgeBodyPost: (anti-cheat-safe) — it reads live RPM and temps from a free monitor you run, instead of shipping a driver of its own. Install either (Compy reads both automatically):
rigViewer.lhmNote: Open-source · runs persistently, no time limit, no setup. Heads-up: its low-level driver can trip strict anti-cheat (Valorant/Vanguard) — close it before those games.
rigViewer.hwinfoNote: Gamer-trusted · turn on “Shared Memory Support” (the free version resets it about every 12 hours).
